mainTopic: The division of ארץ ישראל: the sons of the מרגלים, the בכור's double share for בנות צלפחד, and whether ארץ ישראל counts as מוחזק
overview: This amud deals with how ארץ ישראל was divided, with a focus on בנות צלפחד. First, the גמרא finishes explaining what a פסוק is counting, and learns that בנות צלפחד received their father's בכורה share, so ארץ ישראל counts as already מוחזק. Next it looks at the sons of the מרגלים and מתלוננים. One ברייתא says they took land through their grandfathers, and another says they took it on their own merit. The גמרא gives two answers: the ברייתות follow different views (יוצאי מצרים or באי הארץ), or the difference is whether the son was twenty. Then the גמרא asks how צלפחד could take a double בכור share of land that חפר never held, since a בכור does not take double in ראוי. רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, says the משנה means movable things like tent pegs. רבה rejects this from a ברייתא about the daughters' four land portions, and says instead that ארץ ישראל counts as מוחזק. The גמרא then begins a challenge from a ברייתא of רבי שמעון השקמוני: משה knew the daughters inherit but was unsure about the בכורה share, and the parallel case of the מקושש. That ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse counts fathers' houses and teaches that בנות צלפחד took the בכורה share
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק really is counting בתי אבות. It also teaches that בנות צלפחד received the extra בכורה share, which shows that ארץ ישראל is treated as already owned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the verse is counting fathers' houses. What it comes to teach us is that the daughters of צלפחד took the firstborn's share. This shows that ארץ ישראל is considered already possessed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering a question from just before this section about what the פסוק is counting. It also pulls a new lesson out of that answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a בכור gets a double share only of what his father actually owned (מוחזק), not of what was only coming to him (ראוי). The daughters inherited צלפחד's double בכורה share in his father חפר's land, even though nobody had yet received any land. So the גמרא concludes that ארץ ישראל was treated as if each person already owned it.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (the גמרא keeps its original position)
The extra share a firstborn receives

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that ארץ ישראל counts as מוחזק explains how a בכור could take a double share of land that had not yet been handed out.

phrases.english: Actually, it is counting fathers' houses,
phrases.notes: "It" is the פסוק the גמרא was asking about just before this.

phrases.english: and this is what it teaches us:
that the daughters of Zelophehad took the firstborn's portion;
evidently, Eretz Yisrael is considered already possessed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised right before this section about what the פסוק is counting.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting what the פסוק counts, and drawing a new teaching from it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The count seemed not to fit a count of fathers' houses.
steps.terutzMaskana: It does count fathers' houses. Including בנות צלפחד shows they took the בכורה share, so ארץ ישראל is treated as מוחזק.

steps.title: Did the sons take land through their grandfathers or on their own merit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא saying the sons took land in the merit of their grandfathers. It then challenges it with another ברייתא saying they took land on their own merit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: the sons took a share in the merit of their father's father and their mother's father. But another ברייתא teaches that they took it in their own merit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line of the ברייתא it learned earlier. It shows that a different ברייתא seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sons here are the children of the מרגלים and מתלוננים, who did not receive land themselves. One ברייתא says the children got land through their grandfathers. The other ברייתא says they got land in their own right. Both cannot be true as they stand, so the גמרא needs to explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: In the merit of / by right of

phrases.english: The Master said:
And the sons took in the merit of their fathers' fathers,
phrases.notes: These are the sons of the spies and of the complainers from the earlier ברייתא.

phrases.english: and in the merit of their mothers' fathers.
But isn't it taught: in their own merit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by going back to an earlier ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא saying the sons took land through their grandfathers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא says the sons took land on their own merit, which contradicts it.

steps.title: Each ברייתא follows a different view of who the land was divided among
steps.stepSummary: The two ברייתות follow different opinions. One holds the land was divided among those who left מצרים, and the other holds it was divided among those who entered the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: No difficulty. This ברייתא follows the one who says the land was divided among those who left מצרים. That ברייתא follows the one who says it was divided among those who entered the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each ברייתא follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the land went by יוצאי מצרים, the share belonged to the grandfathers who left מצרים, and the sons received it through them. If the land went by באי הארץ, the sons themselves entered the land, so they took a share on their own merit.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

steps.confusionAlert: Neither ברייתא is wrong. Each is correct according to its own view of how the land was divided.

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
this is according to the one who says it was divided among those who left Egypt,
that is according to the one who says it was divided among those who entered the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; הָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר לְיוֹצְאֵי מִצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two sources follow different opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to directly contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Grandfathers' merit fits the יוצאי מצרים view. Own merit fits the באי הארץ view.

steps.title: Both follow באי הארץ: the difference is whether the son was twenty
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: both ברייתות follow the view that the land was divided among those who entered it. One is talking about a son who was twenty, and the other about a son who was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say both follow the view that the land was divided among those who entered it, and there is no difficulty. This one is about a son who was twenty years old. That one is about a son who was not twenty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to answer the same contradiction, this time keeping both ברייתות within one opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the באי הארץ view, a son who was twenty when they entered the land got his own share, so he took it on his own merit. A son who was not yet twenty had no share of his own, so he took one through his grandfathers. The different ages explain the two ברייתות.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces another answer)
This one and that one, meaning both

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to the contradiction: (1) the ברייתות follow different views, יוצאי מצרים or באי הארץ; (2) both follow באי הארץ, and the difference is whether the son was twenty.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
both this and that follow the view that it was divided among those who entered the land,
and it is not difficult;
this is where he was twenty years old,
phrases.notes: Twenty years old at the time the Jewish people entered the land.

phrases.english: that is where he was not twenty years old.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא וְהָא לְבָאֵי הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same contradiction answered in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two sources describe different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed the ברייתות must follow two different opinions.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow באי הארץ. A son of twenty took on his own merit, and a younger son took through his grandfathers.

steps.title: How could צלפחד take a double share of property that was only ראוי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה saying צלפחד took two shares because he was a בכור. It asks how this is possible, since חפר's land was only ראוי, and a בכור does not take a double share of ראוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: and because he was a firstborn, he took two shares. But why? That property was only due to come to the father, and a firstborn does not take a double share of property that is only due as he does of property already owned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה and challenges it using a known rule about the בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חפר never actually held his share of the land, so that land was only ראוי, meaning due to come to him. The rule is that a בכור takes a double share only of מוחזק, property the father actually owned. So how could צלפחד take a double share here?

keyTerms.meaning: Property due to come to the father but not yet owned

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two terms apart. מוחזק means the father already held it. ראוי means it was only due to come to him. The בכור's double share applies only to מוחזק.

phrases.english: "And because he was a firstborn, he takes two portions."
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה, which is talking about צלפחד and his father חפר.

phrases.english: But why? It is property that was only due,
and a firstborn does not take of property that is due as he does of property that is possessed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that צלפחד took two shares as a בכור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Land that חפר never held is ראוי, and a בכור does not take a double share of ראוי.

steps.title: The משנה is talking about tent pegs
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, explains that the double share mentioned in the משנה refers to tent pegs, meaning movable things חפר actually owned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the משנה is talking about tent pegs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by limiting what the משנה is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tent pegs and similar movable items were things חפר really owned, so they were מוחזק. A בכור does get a double share of those. So the משנה's double share was in such items, and the rule about ראוי is not broken.
steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, the double בכורה share in the משנה was in movable things חפר actually owned, like tent pegs. This keeps the rule that a בכור does not take a double share of ראוי. רבה challenges and replaces this answer in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
It is talking about tent pegs.
phrases.notes: Movable things that חפר really owned, so they count as already possessed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בְּיִתְדוֹת אֹהָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a narrower situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to give a double share of land that was only ראוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The double share was in movable property חפר actually owned, which is מוחזק.

steps.title: רבה challenges the tent pegs answer
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes רבי יהודה: בנות צלפחד took four portions, based on a פסוק about portions of land. So the double share could not have been just tent pegs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה objects: רבי יהודה says the daughters of צלפחד took four portions, as the פסוק says, 'And ten portions fell to מנשה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks the answer of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל. That answer said the double share was only tent pegs, but רבה brings a ברייתא showing it was land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of חבלים, measured plots of land in ארץ ישראל. If the daughters' four portions are counted among those land portions, then the בכורה share included land, not just movable things. So the 'tent pegs' answer cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: the daughters of צלפחד, who inherited their father's share
measured portions of land (literally 'ropes,' used to measure land)

phrases.english: Rabba raises an objection:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
The daughters of Tzelafchad took four portions,
as it says: "And ten portions fell to Menashe"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in Step 6 that the double share was only tent pegs.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל, who said the double share was only movable tent pegs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה ties the daughters' portions to the פסוק about land portions of מנשה. So the extra בכורה share must have included real land.

steps.title: רבה: ארץ ישראל counts as already owned
steps.stepSummary: רבה drops the tent pegs answer and says ארץ ישראל was considered already owned by those entitled to it. So חפר's share counts as מוחזק, not ראוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: ארץ ישראל is considered already owned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a new answer to the question from Step 5. חפר's portion of the land was not 'only expected'; it was already his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in Step 5 was that a בכור does not take double in ראוי, property that has not yet come into the father's hands. רבה says ארץ ישראל was already counted as owned by the people entitled to it, even before it was divided. So the land is מוחזק, and the בכור takes double in it after all.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, a new approach replacing the old one
already owned, in the owner's possession
property due to come to someone but not yet in his hands

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that a בכור does not take double in ראוי, only in מוחזק, decides this whole question. רבה's answer moves ארץ ישראל from the ראוי category into the מוחזק category.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said:
Eretz Yisrael is considered already owned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the tent pegs answer, which Step 7 knocked down, with a new answer to the question of Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the legal status of the land: מוחזק rather than ראוי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought חפר's land was only ראוי, so the double share had to be in movable things.
steps.terutzMaskana: ארץ ישראל counts as already owned, so the בכור's double share applies to the land itself.

steps.title: A ברייתא: משה was unsure about the firstborn share
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a challenge from a ברייתא of רבי שמעון השקמוני. משה knew the daughters inherit, but did not know whether they take the בכורה portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: רבי חידקא said that שמעון השקמוני, his colleague among the students of רבי עקיבא, used to say: משה knew that the daughters of צלפחד inherit, but he did not know whether they take the firstborn's portion or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a challenge, and it seems aimed at רבה's new answer. The ברייתא is long, so the actual point of the challenge will be spelled out only after the ברייתא finishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was unsure whether the daughters take their father's בכורה share. That doubt hints that the answer was not obvious. If ארץ ישראל is clearly מוחזק, as רבה says, it is hard to see why there would be any question at all.

keyTerms.meaning: the extra share of a firstborn

steps.confusionAlert: משה did know that the daughters inherit. His only doubt was about the extra בכורה share of their father, not about inheriting in general.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi Chidka said:
Shimon HaShikmoni was a colleague of mine
among the students of Rabbi Akiva,

phrases.aramaic: וְכָךְ הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הַשִּׁקְמוֹנִי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: and this is what Rabbi Shimon HaShikmoni would say:
Moshe our teacher knew
that the daughters of Tzelafchad are heirs,
but he did not know

phrases.aramaic: אִם נוֹטְלוֹת חֵלֶק בְּכוֹרָה אִם לָאו;
phrases.english: whether they take the firstborn's portion or not;
phrases.notes: Their father צלפחד was חפר's firstborn, so the question is whether his extra share passes to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that seems to challenge רבה's claim in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that ארץ ישראל is מוחזקת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה had a real doubt about the בכורה share. If the land were plainly מוחזק, the answer would have been obvious. The full argument comes after the ברייתא ends.

steps.title: The inheritance section was written through the daughters' merit
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the Torah section about inheritance could have been given directly through משה. The daughters of צלפחד merited that it came through them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The section of inheritances was fit to be written through משה, but the daughters of צלפחד merited, and it was written through them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the same ברייתא. This line adds a side teaching about why the inheritance laws came through the daughters' story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These laws could have been taught as a plain command to משה. Instead they were written as an answer to the daughters' request, because they earned that honor. This line does not change the challenge; it is part of the ברייתא being quoted.

phrases.english: And the section of inheritances was fit
to be written through Moshe,
but the daughters of Tzelafchad merited,
and it was written through them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The inheritance section came through the daughters of צלפחד because they merited it.

steps.title: The parallel case of the wood-gatherer
steps.stepSummary: משה knew the מקושש deserved death but not which kind of death. That section was also written through the person involved, because he became guilty. The sentence leads into a lesson ('to teach you').
steps.simpleTranslation: משה also knew that the wood-gatherer deserved death, as it says, 'Those who desecrate it shall surely be put to death,' but he did not know which death. That section was fit to be written through משה, but the wood-gatherer became guilty and it was written through him, to teach you...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a matching example: the man who gathered wood on שבת. The line ends with 'to teach you,' which sets up a lesson that continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as with the daughters. משה knew the basic law but not one detail, and the Torah section came through the people in the story. The daughters earned it by merit, while the מקושש brought it about through his guilt.

keyTerms.meaning: the man who gathered wood on שבת
those who desecrate it (שבת) shall surely be put to death
by which kind of death penalty

phrases.english: And Moshe our teacher knew
that the wood-gatherer is liable to death,
phrases.notes: The man who gathered wood on שבת, במדבר 15:32–36.

phrases.english: as it says: "Those who desecrate it shall surely be put to death,"
but he did not know
by which death he should die;
and the section of the wood-gatherer was fit
to be written through Moshe,
but the wood-gatherer became guilty,
and it was written through him.
to teach you,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיוֹדֵעַ הָיָה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ שֶׁהַמְקוֹשֵׁשׁ בְּמִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a matching example to the daughters of צלפחד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה knew the מקושש deserved death but not which kind, and that section came through the מקושש because he became guilty.
